- max_tokens and reasoning_effort=none keep Groq inside its free-tier limits

agents/llm.py.title: observation_message: the finish reminder
note: **Wraps each tool result with 'answer now or call one more tool'.**
- Small models otherwise keep calling tools after they have the answer
- On the last allowed step it insists on a final answer

agents/llm.py.title: extract_json: tolerant parsing
note: **Pulls the first balanced {...} out of a reply, even wrapped in prose or a code fence.**
- Returns None if nothing parses - the loop then asks the model to retry

agents/llm.py.title: which_backend: reporting only
note: **Tells you (and the run banner) which backend chat() will use.**

agents/simple_agent.py.title: The tool registry
note: **Everything the model will ever know about a tool comes from these descriptions.**
- name -> function, plus prose and an args dict
- build_system_prompt turns this into text; the model never sees the code

agents/cli_agent.py.title: Job 2: a timeout
note: **A hung command must not hang the agent - kill it after two minutes.**

agents/cli_agent.py.title: Job 1 and 4: capture, then format
note: **Exit code, stdout and stderr go to the model as one labelled text block.**
- The exit code is the only structured signal a raw CLI gives us

agents/cli_agent.py.title: Job 3: truncate
note: **Long output is cut at MAX_OUTPUT so one pytest run can't fill the model's context.**
- Arbitrary truncation is exactly what Lab 3 designs away

cli_tools/repo_tool.py.title: do_tests: the worked example
note: **Runs pytest and returns a small JSON dict instead of a screen of text.**
- ok/passed/failed/failures: the shape every other subcommand copies
- Model it when you merge do_search, do_log_summary and do_ticket

mcp_server/repo_mcp.py.title: search_code: the worked example
note: **One decorator turns a typed Python function into an MCP tool.**
- Name, description (docstring) and input schema (type hints) are generated
- The body is a one-line call into the Lab 3 logic - same capability, new surface

mcp_server/try_server.py.title: 1. Launch the server
note: **The client starts the server as a subprocess and talks to it over stdin/stdout.**
- No import, no URL - only a script path

mcp_server/try_server.py.title: 2. Handshake
note: **initialize() is the protocol handshake - versions and capabilities are exchanged.**

mcp_server/try_server.py.title: 3. Discover tools
note: **The server advertises its tools; the client learns names, descriptions and schemas at runtime.**
- This is what lets the Lab 6 agent work with any server unchanged

mcp_server/try_server.py.title: 4. Call a tool
note: **A call is a name plus a JSON argument object - the same shape the agent will emit.**
- The result comes back as content parts; text parts carry the JSON

agents/mcp_agent.py.title: (a) No import - only a script path
note: **The agent never imports the server; it launches whatever script you point it at.**
- Lab 8 swaps in git_mcp.py with --server and nothing else changes

agents/mcp_agent.py.title: (b) Prompt built from discovery
note: **Tool names, descriptions and schemas come from list_tools(), not from code.**

agents/mcp_agent.py.title: (c) Errors travel in-protocol
note: **A failed call is flagged with is_error and still returns text the model can react to.**

agents/compare_agents.py.title: Same task, two surfaces
note: **Runs the Lab 4 (CLI) and Lab 6 (MCP) agents back to back on one task.**
- Same model, same loop - only the tool surface differs

agents/compare_agents.py.anchor: steps = sum(1 for line in transcript.splitlines() if line.startswith("--- step"))
agents/compare_agents.py.title: Counting tool calls
note: **Tool calls are counted from the captured transcript's '--- step' lines.**

agents/compare_agents.py.title: Transcripts to compare
note: **Each run's full transcript lands in transcripts/ - open both side by side in step 3.**

mcp_server/git_mcp.py.title: The allowlist
note: **Enumerate goodness: only these read-only subcommands can ever run.**
- push, commit, reset... are refused by name, with the allowed list in the error

mcp_server/git_mcp.py.title: _git: the one place that shells out
note: **Every tool funnels through here - timeout, error capture and truncation live once.**

mcp_server/git_mcp.py.title: recent_commits: a narrow, single-question tool
note: **One question, no git flags exposed - the model can't misuse what it can't reach.**
- Turns git log text into structured commit dicts
- Compare with git_readonly, the flexible-but-guarded general-purpose tool you merge in

guardrails/policy.py.title: Control point 1: allowlist
note: **Only these tools may run, whatever the server advertises.**

guardrails/policy.py.title: Control point 2: human approval
note: **Side-effecting tools stop and ask you before executing - the [y/N] prompt in step 4.**

guardrails/policy.py.title: Control point 3: validation
note: **Checks a proposed call against the allowlist and the tool's own schema.**
- Missing/unexpected arguments and oversized strings are rejected with a reason
- The reason goes back to the model as a DENIED observation

guardrails/policy.py.title: Control point 4: audit log
note: **One JSON line per decision in audit_log.jsonl - you read it in step 5.**
- Executed, denied, approved_by_human, rejected_by_human all land here

eval/scenarios.json.title: A scenario is a task...
note: **Each scenario gives the agent one realistic task - the same kind you ran in earlier labs.**

eval/scenarios.json.title: ...plus checks that are plain code
note: **Checks are facts, not opinions: the answer names the test, within a step budget.**
- No LLM judging the LLM - every check is code you merge in step 2
- Types: final_contains, final_not_empty, ticket_created, max_tool_calls
